control_plane_hardening_items.why_a_lane_cannot_fix_it: .github/** is control-plane scope and is never edited from a lane, a team or the director.
intended_upstream_fix_for_the_control_pl: emit the offending paths in the annotation's raw_details (the `echo -e "::error::auditor crossed scope:\n$BAD"` text is not surfaced today, so the failure is undiagnosable from outside)
give the audit job the same 'Clean generated junk' step the team job has, or run the scope check against an explicit allow-list of the two directories after a cleanup pass
persist the audit snapshot with `if: always()` so an out-of-scope write is still inspectable instead of vanishing
make the 'Independent audit' prompt state that scratch/recompute output must go to a temp directory outside the checkout, since the guard cannot distinguish scratch from a verdict file
control_plane_hardening_items.route_around_used: the producer hands the auditor a complete, self-describing snapshot (report of record, machine-readable artifacts, an executable re-derivation test) so no scratch file inside the checkout should be needed; and this lane records the diagnosis rather than retrying the identical dispatch.

control_plane_hardening_items.gap: .github/workflows/core-lane.yml job 'team': step 'Enforce lane write scope' inspects only `git status --porcelain -uall` (PENDING changes), while step 'Persist team snapshot' is guarded by `if: always()` and force-pushes `git add -A`. A producer that writes an auditor-namespace path therefore fails the guard (run 40163751502, exit 3) and is published ANYWAY; the next operational resume then inherits those bytes as committed content, at which point the pending-only guard passes and the pollution becomes permanent in the chain (run 40164459036, team=success).
